prompt: Which mathematical expression correctly defines the root-mean-square speed c_rms of N gas molecules having individual speeds c_1, c_2, ..., c_N?

answer.explanation: Root-mean-square speed is defined as the square root of the mean of the squares of the speeds: c_rms = sqrt(<c^2>) = sqrt((1/N) * sum(c_i^2)).

distractor_explanations: Option 1 is correct: root-mean-square speed is the square root of the arithmetic mean of the squared speeds.
Option 2 is incorrect: this is the arithmetic mean speed <c>, not the root-mean-square speed.
Option 3 is incorrect: this is the square of the mean speed (<c>)^2.
Option 4 is incorrect: this is the square root of the mean speed, which does not have the correct physical definition or dimensions of speed.
hints: Read the name in reverse: Square the speeds, take the Mean, then take the square Root.
Distinguish between mean-square speed and root-mean-square speed.
solution: The root-mean-square speed is obtained by squaring each speed, finding the mean of these squares, and then taking the square root: c_rms = sqrt((c_1^2 + c_2^2 + ... + c_N^2) / N). Option A is correct.
teacher_walkthrough: Clarify the operations in order: square, mean, root.
Write out the formula: c_rms = sqrt(<c^2>).
Highlight that c_rms is always slightly larger than the arithmetic mean speed <c> for any non-uniform distribution.
